title: Keep one catalog entry per runnable test
statement: As a developer, I can count on each catalog entry being one test I can run, so what the catalog says it has, and how long it takes, matches what really happens.
overview: Trevor asked what makes most sense. A `test()` is what runs, what costs money, what flakes and what is positive or negative, so it is the honest unit. Today's 27 end-to-end test cases reach 16 distinct `test()` blocks, by a rough parse, and 8 of those blocks are claimed by more than one case. A test case can already verify several criteria across features, so merging those cases into one needs no new record. Non-end-to-end test cases are not held to this.

acceptance_criteria.statement: The catalog reports a test case that declares more than one test, or none.
The catalog reports two test cases that declare the same test.
Catalog counts are of distinct tests, not of test cases.
These reports fail nothing, and existing test cases stay valid.
An entry is one test case, and that case may verify criteria from any feature.
